name: ambilight-follows-a-changing-page
description:
the glow follows the page while its content changes, with no navigation and no tab switch. The fixture's left half sweeps from crimson to green over six seconds under a CSS animation, so the only thing that moves between the two captures is the page's own pixels.

Every other scenario in this family changes the page by loading a different one. This is the one that proves the sampler is a LOOP rather than an event handler with extra steps - nothing commits, nothing is clicked, and the chrome still moves.

actions.note: the page commits and the animation starts
the glow near the crimson end of the sweep
the sweep runs on. No navigation, no click, no tab switch.
the glow near the green end of the sweep

assertions.label: nothing-navigated-in-between
assertions.desc: THE CONTROL: exactly one commit in the whole run, so the change measured below cannot be a page load. A ceiling alone would pass on a run where nothing loaded at all, which is why the floor is 1.
THE MEASUREMENT: the sidebar followed the page's left half from crimson toward green while nothing but the page's own animation ran. An event-driven sampler measures zero here.
assertions.note: The band the glow paints: 32 DIP out from the card's left edge at about x=225 in the VM frame, at 55 percent of the glass alpha. Re-measured 2026-08-27 when the glow was narrowed and dimmed.
